name: Glycolysis, Pyruvate Dehydrogenase and the TCA Cycle
hyTerms: X-linked cause of congenital lactic acidosis

reference.source: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry / Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
clinicalPearls: Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) is the rate-limiting commitment step of glycolysis; inhibited by ATP and citrate; activated by AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate
Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate is synthesized by PFK-2; insulin dephosphorylates and activates PFK-2, promoting glycolysis; glucagon phosphorylates and activates FBPase-2
Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex requires 5 cofactors: Thiamine (B1), Lipoic acid, Coenzyme A (B5), FAD (B2), NAD+ (B3)
PDH deficiency is an X-linked cause of congenital lactic acidosis; arsenic inhibits lipoic acid, causing cellular energy depletion
TCA cycle generates 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP and 2 CO2 per turn; rate-limiting enzyme is isocitrate dehydrogenase
reference.pathophysiology: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency results in pyruvate accumulation and shunting to lactate via lactate dehydrogenase, causing severe neonatal lactic acidosis and psychomotor retardation. Arsenic binds lipoic acid sulfhydryls, halting both PDH and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase. Fluoroacetate inhibits aconitase, arresting the citric acid cycle.
additionalDifferentials: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS)
additionalInvestigations: Plasma lactate and pyruvate ratio (normal <20; elevated in mitochondrial respiratory chain defects)
Urine organic acid analysis via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
